chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a man who caught a fish, tied it with a thread, and sent it in the water, so it died. Can it be eaten? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Is fish caught by tying it with a thread and letting it die in the water permissible to eat?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a fish caught by baiting and tethering becomes impermissible if it dies while still submerged and not yet retrieved, distinguishing it from fish caught by net or hook where death in water is permissible. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the method of capture and the state of the animal at the moment of death, ensuring the 'sacrifice' is complete and valid for consumption.
